best_plan.name: p5
best_plan.rationale: p5 achieved perfect quality (f1_score 1.0) while costing much less than the other perfect-quality plans. Compared with p2 and p4, it kept the same quality but reduced cost substantially, and it was also cheaper than p6 while being much more accurate. It uses cheap GPT-4.1-Nano sentiment filters for positive/negative review selection and a low-cost Gemini Flash Lite join to pair different reviews, giving the best observed cost-quality trade-off.

plan_codes.p1:
left = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_left", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
left.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
left.sem_filter(
    "This review is overall positive about the movie.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)

right = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_right", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
right.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
right.sem_filter(
    "This review is overall negative about the movie.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)

pipeline = left.sem_join(
    right,
    "These are two different reviews of the same movie; keep the pair.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE
)
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["reviewId"] != row["reviewId_right"])
pipeline.project(["idx", "reviewId", "reviewId_right"])
pipeline.limit(10)
pipeline
